newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief thanks Kabila but warns of deadlines.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief thanks Kabila but warns of deadlines.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Monday complimented rebel leader Laurent Kabila for his intervention in the Rwandan refugee crisis but at the same time warned him about setting a deadline for their repatriation.

Annan, who has been sharply critical of Kabila, said in a statement that he was encouraged and pleased that the rebel leader had gone to Kisangani in eastern Zaire over the weekend to take personal charge of the situation.

But Annan's spokesman, Fred Eckhard, in answer to questions, rejected Kabila's comments on Saturday in which he set a 60-day deadline to repatriate all the refugees in Zaire or "we will do it ourselves."

"If you are talking about 60 days from now, that is an unrealistic deadline," Eckhard said. He said 60 days appeared "doable" only after the refugees had been found, relocated to a secure place, fed and given medical care.
Eckhard also deflected Kabila's demand that Annan apologise personally to him for describing the fate of Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire as "slow extermination."
"We understand Mr Kabila is under a lot of pressure these days," Eckhard said.

At issue was the refusal of rebel leaders in eastern Zaire to grant access to the refugees by humanitarian groups, journalists and other foreigners. When U.N. officials finally managed to visit one camp last week, they found more than 50,000 refugees had disappeared.
On Monday, aid officials and journalists who visited Biaro, 25 miles south of Kisangani city, saw about 5,000 refugees drifting out of the forest back to their camps.

At the same time UNICEF, the U.N. Children's Fund, reported that on Saturday, about 50 ailing Hutu refugee children were seized from a hospital in rebel-held territory. The were being treated for malnutrition.

About two million Rwandan Hutus fled their country in 1994, fearing retribution after the country's then Hutu army and militias launched a campaign of genocide against the minority Tutsis. They were then defeated by the forces of the Tutsi-led Patriotic Front.
Many refugees returned to Rwanda at the end of last year but about 250,000 fled westwards before the advance of the Zairean rebels, allied with the Rwandan government.

In his statement, Annan said that humanitarian agencies "will need the support of Mr Kabila and that of his alliance, to locate and gain access to the refugees, gather them to points where they can receive aid and be secure and eventually repatriate them to Rwanda."
He said the entire international community was counting on Kabila's support for a successful relief operation and would "continue to monitor the situation closely."
